This page shows the exact spawn multipliers, the Port payback in two trade-ship arrivals, the Factory payback in the late game, and the two numeric scenarios that decide the order.\n\n Economy Difficulty · Intermediate Published Sep 22, 2026 Updated Sep 22, 2026 Reviewed by OpenFront Intel editors #port#factory#trade#train#spawn#economy#timing#v0.34.12#gold#investment#strategy \n\nFreshness check\n\nSite baseline\n...\nChecked against the v0.34.12 tag (commit 7c27263, released 2026-09-20). The only change to the two spawn curves is the damping midpoint: tradeShipSaturation moved from sigmoid midpoint 230 to 330, trainSaturation from 500 to 560; the boost terms (1 plus 0.45 times exp minus ships over 40 for trade, 1 plus 0.5 times exp minus units over 30 for trains) and the plateau terms (0.25 times 1 minus sigmoid, trade knee 900, train knee 900) are byte-identical. Port and Factory each cost 125,000 gold; tradeShipGold is 75,000 over 1 plus exp minus 0.03 times (distance minus debuff) plus 50 times distance; trainGold is 10,000 self, 25,000 team, 35,000 ally with the first nine cities free then 5,000 per city floored at 5,000. Verified 2026-09-22.\n...\nThe single most useful reframe of v0.34.12 is that the faster trade-ship and train spawns are not a bigger pie, they are an earlier slice. The release raised two spawn-saturation midpoints and left everything else untouched, so the total gold you will ever collect over a full game is roughly the same, but a meaningful share of it now arrives during the mid-game instead of the late game. That changes when you should make your first two capital investments, not whether. Concretely: buy your first Port early enough that you are already collecting the buff while the map is in the 150-to-400-trade-ship window, and hold the Factory until the late game, because the trade-ship buff peaks near 300 ships at roughly double the v0.34.11 rate while the train buff only reaches its modest peak near 700 units. If you take one action from this page, make it this: do not defer your first Port to the late game. The Port is the fast lever, it pays back in about two trade-ship arrivals, and it is the one that actually benefits from the v0.34.12 change. The Factory is the slow lever; it pays back over many train visits and its buff arrives later and weaker, so it stays a later, more conservative purchase. The table below maps the board signals to the decision, and every number that follows is pulled from the v0.34.12 source, not from memory or from a patch notes summary.\n...\nPrecision matters here because the community keeps describing this patch as “more ships spawn” or “the economy got a buff,” and both of those are half-right in a way that will mislead your build order if you stop at the headline. The v0.34.12 source changes exactly two numbers in exactly two functions, and both changes push the spawn rate up in the mid-game.
